objective: Replace the architectural role of Neuro's avatar module with a real optional VTube Studio adapter for Hina, exposing safe operator controls for the selected Live2D model while preserving the transparent VRM widget as the offline fallback.
non_goals: Do not copy or redistribute the Hiyori sample model or claim that Neuro's MIT license covers it.
Do not require VTube Studio for normal desktop startup or remove the current VRM fallback.
Do not expose arbitrary VTube Studio API payloads, filesystem paths or plugin tokens to the renderer.
Do not add Twitch, song or game controls whose backends do not yet exist.
contracts: Only the Electron main process connects to the loopback VTube Studio public API; renderer access is a fixed typed operator-only IPC allowlist.
The one-time authentication token is stored locally, bounded and never logged or returned to the renderer.
Connection, current model, hotkeys and movement presets have timeouts and stable disconnected/error states.
VTube Studio absence or failure never prevents desktop startup, chat, voice or the existing transparent VRM widget.
The dashboard identifies Hiyori as an external separately licensed sample and does not imply that Hina bundles it.
allowed_dependencies: Node 24 built-in WebSocket implementation and the official VTube Studio public API; no new npm dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A fake WebSocket unit test covers connect, authentication, token redaction, model status, hotkey trigger, movement preset, timeout and disconnect.
Desktop typecheck/build and IPC smoke prove the fixed preload surface without arbitrary channel access.
The Avatar dashboard gives non-developers installation, authorization, Hiyori license and fallback guidance plus real status/hotkey/movement controls.
When VTube Studio is unavailable the page reports an actionable offline state and the VRM widget remains usable.
